EDR-Bot: [ALERT] High severity - Suspicious scheduled task created on HOST-AL-KIM (Windows 10)
EDR-Bot: Rule: Persistence: Scheduled Task - observed creating task 'Updater' -> payload C:\Users\alex\AppData\Local\Temp\updaterd.exe (quarantined).
EDR-Bot: SHA256: d4f7c3a9b1e2f9a3e8aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00. Outbound blocked to 45.32.10.77. Alert: 1768504321.

Alex Kim: that's my dev laptop, I'm remote at home now. I didn't install anything called updaterd. just ran npm + yarn earlier.

Samira Patel: thanks Alex. please don't access any internal services until we triage. @Mike R. can you isolate host in EDR (network quarantine)? also need device serial & corp VPN status.

Mike R.: isolating host now -> network quarantine applied (EDR action ID: nq-17685). kicking off remote full scan and file collection. Alex: are you on corp VPN or split-tunnel? if yes, disconnect until we confirm.

Jess Ortega: Alex — please run these and paste outputs (only the outputs, avoid screenshots):
```
whoami
wmic bios get serialnumber
schtasks /query /fo LIST /v | findstr /i "Updater"
powershell -Command "Get-Process -Id (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName Updater).Actions"
certutil -hashfile C:\Users\alex\AppData\Local\Temp\updaterd.exe SHA256
```
If the Get-ScheduledTask command errors, paste schtasks output.

Alex Kim: serial: ABC12345XYZ
on VPN: yes (CorpVPN via globalprotect, split-tunnel)
schtasks shows: TaskName: \Updater, Next Run Time: 3/15/2026 03:14:00 AM, Author: SYSTEM, Action: C:\Users\alex\AppData\Local\Temp\updaterd.exe
certutil: d4f7c3a9b1e2f9a3e8aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00
remote scan started, will update when done.

EDR-Bot: Additional artifact: child process attempted DNS lookup to suspicious domain xn--update-checker[.]com and outbound TCP conn to 45.32.10.77:443 (blocked). File has no valid signature. Reputation: unknown -> flagged as malicious by heuristic.

Samira Patel: given persistence + outbound attempts, recommend full forensic capture + reimage. Policy: user-dev-laptop with SYSTEM author + scheduled task = compromise. @Mike R. please arrange SAN image via forensics team. Also notify People Ops for user device replacement and manager.

Mike R.: acknowledged. creating Forensics ticket FS-2026-128, starting disk collection (EDR script to collect memory, scheduled task XML, event logs). Alex: we will schedule a courier if you need a replacement device.

Jess Ortega: action items: 1) Forensics capture in progress (FS-2026-128), 2) Host quarantined network-wise, 3) User advised to stop VPN & corporate access, 4) Reimage recommended, 5) Notify infra/credentials teams to rotate any tokens used from this host. I'll open an incident slack channel and post the summary to #incidents.

Alex Kim: thanks all — i'm available for handoff and can drop off laptop if courier arranged.

Samira Patel: will follow up with post-incident questions (possible attacker vector: malicious npm package vs binary dropped by script). tagging @devex to audit recent CI/npm installs for alex.

EDR-Bot: Alert closed by analyst (Samira) pending forensic results. timeline: detection -> quarantine -> capture started.
